title: Prophet Ibrahim and the Fire
summary: The story of Prophet Ibrahim 'alaihis salam, who sought God with his reason, rejected idols, and was saved by Allah from the blazing fire. (QS. Al-An'am: 74-79; QS. Al-Anbiya: 51-70; Bukhari)
moral: Be brave in defending the truth, put your trust in Allah, and be sure that His help comes in ways we do not expect.
pages: Prophet Ibrahim 'alaihis salam was born among a people who worshipped statues of stone. Since childhood he wondered in his heart, 'Can these things that cannot hear, see, or help be worthy of worship?'
One night he saw a star and said, 'Is this my Lord?' But when the star set, he said, 'I do not love things that set.' Then the moon rose, but the moon also set. (QS. Al-An'am: 76-77)
When the sun rose brightly, he said, 'Is this my Lord? This is greater.' But the sun set too. Then he said, 'I turn my face to the One who created the heavens and the earth.' (QS. Al-An'am: 78-79)
Prophet Ibrahim gently advised his father and his people to leave the idols. But they refused. When his people were away, the idols were found smashed, and they became angry.
They said, 'Burn him and help your gods.' (QS. Al-Anbiya: 68). So they gathered firewood and lit a huge fire, so that its smoke and heat could be felt from afar.
When he was thrown into the fire, Prophet Ibrahim said, 'Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil', meaning, 'Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Protector.' (Bukhari). He relied only on Allah.
Allah said, 'O fire, be cool, and be safety for Ibrahim!' (QS. Al-Anbiya: 69). At once the fire became cool, and Prophet Ibrahim was saved by Allah's permission.
They wanted to plot evil, but Allah made them the losers. From this story we learn: to bravely defend the truth, to trust in Allah, and to be sure that His help comes in beautiful ways. The end.
